benchmarks.name: alu.throughput

negative_control.detail: every kernel <= 512 op/core/clk; all 18 kernels: 2x iterations -> 1.85..2.15x time; fp32 fma indep/dep = 5.145; results match the CPU model

benchmarks.notes: per_core_clk assumes the top P-state (1620 MHz): see gpu.top_state_share; FMA counted as 2 FLOP (TFLOPS) and 1 op (per_core_clk); i32 add = add + xor pairs; library in MathModeSafe
benchmarks.title: FP32/FP16/INT32 FMA, ADD, MUL: dependent vs independent chains

benchmarks.name: alu.dual_issue

negative_control.detail: f16+f32+i32 mix 2x iterations -> 1.976x time (want 1.85..2.15, tries 1); all results match the CPU model; f32x32 / f32x16 time = 2.014 (want 1.3..2.4: doubling the work cannot be free nor more than 2.4x; the lower bound is loose because shader validation leaves 16 chains unsaturated, tries 1); every kernel <= 512 op/core/clk

benchmarks.notes: ratio = time(mix) / sum(time(parts)), same iterations and threads: 1 = no overlap, 0.5 = perfect overlap of two parts, <1 = concurrent issue; mixes use 8 independent chains per type per thread; headline ratios at 256 threads/threadgroup; f16x2 = packed half2 FMA (2 lanes per op); occupancy knob: dynamic threadgroup memory per 128-thread threadgroup limits resident threadgroups; library in MathModeSafe; per_core_clk assumes the top P-state (1620 MHz): see gpu.top_state_share
benchmarks.title: FP16/FP32/INT32 mixes vs parts by SIMD-groups per threadgroup; FP16 vs FP32 ILP

benchmarks.name: alu.transcendental

negative_control.detail: sin.fast 2x iterations -> 1.983x time (want 1.85..2.15, tries 1); all float results within tolerance of the double fixed point, ints exact; every op kernel >= its glue (fma only) kernel; no precise:: op more than 10% faster than fast::

benchmarks.notes: all times are MINIMA of the repetitions (other GPU clients only add time); throughput metric value = minimum-time based; cost of an op = t(op kernel) - t(glue kernel = fma only) at equal iterations; fma_equiv = that time / time of one FP32 FMA per link (same iterations), i.e. the op's cost in FP32 FMAs; raw times in params; chains: v = op(fma(v,a,b)), 8 per thread, contraction with a fixed point in the domain of the op; float results checked against the double fixed point (1-4% tolerance, approximations differ from CPU), ints bit-exact; modes: precise:: / fast:: (library in MathModeSafe) ; f16 = half overloads ; default_fastmath = plain calls compiled with fast math ON (Xcode default); rcp = 1.0f/v, div = c/v with runtime c; integer: x = x*K+C; x ^= r(x); base = mad + xor with a runtime value; udiv_c7 = constant divisor (mul-high), *_rt runtime divisor 7; f32.transcendental.* = median Top/s of rcp, rsqrt, exp2, log2, sin, cos
benchmarks.title: rcp/rsqrt/sqrt/exp2/log2/sin/cos/pow/div: precise vs fast vs half; int div/mod vs shift

benchmarks.name: occupancy.registers

negative_control.detail: alu N=32 2x rounds -> 2.064x time (want 1.85..2.15, tries 1); all results match the CPU model; dynamically indexed array (stack) N=32 takes 62.59x the register version (want > 1.3)

benchmarks.notes: regs_<N> = FMA Top/s with 16 dependent gather loads per thread from a 64 MiB table (latency exposed unless other threads hide it) and ~16K FMAs per thread; regs_alu_<N> = same without loads (compiler spills only); values are minimum-time based; thrashing_point.live_regs = smallest N > 96 (else 48 or 64) with throughput < 80% of the reference (median of N=16,32,48,64,96); 0 = none up to N=256 (found=0); compare with thrashing_point_alu to separate spills from occupancy loss; lat_regs_<N> = loads/s with 1 FMA round per load (64 loads per thread, latency-bound); inflight_threads_per_core.regs_<N> = loads/s x single-SIMD-group load latency / cores = ESTIMATED resident threads per core (Little), valid only where alu_bound = 0 and once the estimate has saturated; max_threads_tg.regs_<N> = pipeline maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup (drops when the compiler reports high register use); resident threads per core are not observable directly
benchmarks.title: Live registers vs throughput, thrashing point of the dynamic register file

benchmarks.name: threadgroup.memory

negative_control.detail: stride 32 / stride 1 time = 5.183 (must not be < 0.95); stride 1 2x iterations -> 1.975x (1.6..2.3, tries 1); all results match the CPU; latency 32.974 ns in (1, 500); increments of 1x/2x steps consistent: ratio 0.867 (0.7..1.4)

benchmarks.notes: tg_bw: 256-thread threadgroups, each thread reads 8 uint per iteration from a 16 KiB threadgroup array at index lane*stride + uniform offset (mod 4096); bank conflicts appear as time growth with stride (32 banks x 4 B assumed, stride 33 = conflict free); GB/s of loads only, whole GPU; tg_latency: one thread chases a random single-cycle permutation held in threadgroup memory; (t(3n)-t(n))/2n removes fill and launch costs; min-based value in tg_latency.min_based; tg_time_ratio.stride_k = min time relative to stride 1
benchmarks.title: Threadgroup memory: bandwidth by stride (bank conflicts) and latency

benchmarks.name: simd.ops

negative_control.detail: sg_shuffle 2x iterations -> 1.981x (1.85..2.15, tries 1); all sg_/tg_/dv_ results match the CPU model; if/else 50% taken = 1.849x of 0% (both bodies run, want > 1.3); 100% = 1.071x (0.7..1.4); if-only 25% = 1.000x of 100% (want > 0.8), 0% = 0.177x (want < 0.5), tries 1

benchmarks.notes: threadgroup-memory emulation was more than 2x FASTER than the intrinsic for: shuffle ; simd.<op> / tg.<op> = SIMD-group instructions per second (threads/32 x iters x 4 chains), each link = the op + one cheap ALU op (glue); speedup.<op> = time(tg) / time(simd) (>1: intrinsic faster); tg emulation uses simdgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup): shuffle = write+read, sum = 5-step tree, prefix = Hillis-Steele scan, ballot = tree sum of pred<<lane; quad_shuffle = xor 1/2 neighbour; divergence: lanes take the branch when ((lane*13)&31) < n; bodies = 8 rounds of 4 FMA chains; ifelse ratios vs 0% taken, ifonly ratios vs 100% taken; minimum-time based
benchmarks.title: SIMD-group ops vs threadgroup-memory equivalents; divergence cost

benchmarks.name: atomics

negative_control.detail: dev n1024 2x iterations -> 2.015x time (1.7..2.3, tries 1); counters, returned-value sums, 64-bit max/min and compaction outputs exact; per-thread-address rate 219.31 vs single address 1.5839 Gop/s (want > 2x); 1024 addresses 34.991 (want > 2x single); naive compaction 0.3497 ms vs simd 0.3508 ms (reported, not asserted)

benchmarks.notes: dev: atomic_fetch_add(+1) relaxed on address (gid & (naddr-1)) * stride words; padded = 32 words (128 B), unpadded = 1 word; 2^18 threads; tg: 2^20 threads in 256-thread groups, threadgroup atomic_uint; 64-bit: MSL 4 provides only atomic_max_explicit/atomic_min_explicit (no return value) on device atomic_ulong; add/exchange/fetch_* and threadgroup 64-bit atomics do not compile (metal_atomic header); atomic32.max.* is the same op on 32-bit values; compaction: each thread keeps ~1/2 of its elements; naive = 1 device atomic per kept element, simd = simd_prefix_exclusive_sum + 1 atomic per SIMD-group, simd_tg = 1 tg atomic per SIMD-group + 1 device atomic per threadgroup; Gelem/s counts all input elements; rates in metrics are medians; ratios use minimum times
benchmarks.title: 32/64-bit atomics: device vs threadgroup, contention, hierarchical vs naive compaction

benchmarks.name: memory.hierarchy

negative_control.detail: 1 GiB read 2 passes/1 pass = 1.964x, chase 4N/N steps at the L1 set (want 2.5..6.5) = 3.927x; every kernel result matches the CPU; latency_dram 567 ns vs 5 x latency_l1 150 ns; read curve monotone-ish after the peak: 0 violations (>30% up-step)

benchmarks.notes: slc_size_estimate is a MODEL estimate (h = min(1, C/WS), least squares on the read curve for WS >= 64 MiB), not a measured size; see slc_fit.* for the residual; latency = slope of the minimum times between N and 4N chase steps (15 reps) (128-byte lines, includes TLB effects; a single GPU thread, core unknown: no per-die latency asymmetry test, S-MEM-6 open); onchip_bw = median read bandwidth over 4..32 MiB working sets (GPU-wide, above DRAM); read passes carry a runtime-zero offset so loads cannot be reused; IOReport PMP 'DCS BW' under-reads (spike): not used; random vs zero data at 16 MiB: zeros 0.99x the speed of random data; copy_bw 528 GB/s counts read+write; M5 Max nominal 614 GB/s is an external reference
benchmarks.title: Latency and bandwidth per level (L1, SLC, DRAM), SLC size model fit

benchmarks.name: memory.contention

negative_control.detail: 0-thread GPU read 572 GB/s; repeated at the end 572 GB/s (ratio 1.000, must be within +-10% = same measurement as B-08's dram_bw; plausible range 200..737); no total above 1.6 x nominal 614 GB/s, contended sides never faster than alone; GPU results match the CPU

benchmarks.notes: cpu_bw = memcpy read+write bytes/s (DRAM traffic), threads default QoS, 256 MiB private buffer each (128 MiB -> 128 MiB, 4 MiB chunks); windows shared with the GPU measurements; M5 Max nominal DRAM bandwidth 614 GB/s is an external reference (Apple), not a measured fact; SLC hits may push a total above it; cpu threads are not pinned (macOS has no affinity API): P/E core placement is left to the scheduler
benchmarks.title: CPU memcpy threads vs GPU DRAM streaming: bandwidth of both sides

benchmarks.name: texture.sampling

negative_control.detail: 2x samples -> time x1.986 median (min 1.60, max 2.16; 0 outside 1.5..2.6, allowed 25%: contention outliers) over 48 cases (ratios of minima); sparse < 0.9 x coherent at 8192^2 (point) for 6/6 formats (need >= 5): rgba8=0.01 rgba16f=0.02 rg11b10f=0.01 rgb9e5=0.01 bc7=0.04 astc4x4=0.04 ; per-thread sums match the CPU replay (48 cases x 8 threads, BC7/ASTC checked against AppleTextureEncoder decode)

benchmarks.name: texture.compression

negative_control.detail: 2x passes -> time x2.002 (compute write, plain random), x1.953 (render target); texels read back through a blit (6000 per config and write test) and 6 read-kernel sums per config match the CPU replay of the content function

benchmarks.notes: compression ratio is not measurable (Metal exposes no compression counters, F4.4): only optimized/plain bandwidth deltas are reported as indirect evidence; Apple9 path: shader-written textures are not compressed there, 'optimized' expected equal to 'plain' for compute writes (render targets are compressed on every Apple GPU); optimized/plain ratios: write.constant=1.49 write.smooth=1.30 write.random=0.92 write_partial.smooth=1.77 write_partial.random=1.19 rt_write.smooth=1.10 rt_write.random=0.97 read.smooth=1.56 read.random=0.91 ; optimized = TextureDescriptor.allowGPUOptimizedContents true; plain = false; 4096x4096 RGBA8Unorm private, 4 passes per timed span, bandwidth counts logical bytes written/read (partial: 50%: 2x2 cells in a checkerboard, touching every 4x4 block); render target partial writes not measured: they need loadAction Load (a different experiment); random content = hashed texels, smooth = 16-texel-step gradients, constant = one colour per pass

benchmarks.name: hsr

negative_control.detail: blend.back_to_front (t16-t2)/(t8-t2) = 2.23 (ideal 2.33, accepted 1.6..3.2); hsr.front_to_back added time 1->16 layers 0.032 ms < 0.3 x blend 1.118 ms; read-back: nearest layer visible in opaque/discard variants, last layer in blend+depth-Always (all 8 layers executed)

benchmarks.notes: back-to-front opaque does not scale (0.02 of the blended slope): tile-based HSR removes hidden layers regardless of order; 1 pass 1920x1080 RGBA8+Depth32F, fragment = 36 dependent FMA pairs calibrated to ~0.07 ms per blended layer; span minus empty span

benchmarks.notes: fit over 4 resolutions of the added time per MB: rgba8 hidden GB/s (r2 0.58) rgba16f 3214. GB/s (r2 0.88) rgba32f 732.5 GB/s (r2 0.98) depth32f hidden GB/s (r2 0.96) ; a small render pass between compute encoders costs either ~15 or ~60 us (bimodal: see empty_pass.us min vs median); cells = median over rounds of the per-round MINIMUM, so every variant is compared in the fast mode; pass = clear|load + full-screen triangle writing an incompressible per-pixel hash + store|dontCare (A dontcare, B store, E/C: same with a discard-1-pixel-in-4 draw, clear/load); store.<k> = bytes/(B - empty pass), load.<k> = bytes/(C - empty pass); load_added = C - E, store_added = B - A; span minus empty span; empty_pass.us = 64x64 RGBA8 clear+dontCare with one full-screen triangle of 4096 pixels (a pass with no side effect is flagged by the validation layer), minus the empty CommandTimer span; chain32 = 32 such passes in one command buffer / 32

benchmarks.name: imageblock

negative_control.detail: the size after the maximum fails: tile_32x32 max 24 B, 28 B refused (pipeline created and pass completed without error, but the t) tile_32x16 max 56 B, 60 B refused (pipeline created and pass completed without error, but the t) tile_16x16 max 56 B, 60 B refused (pipeline created and pass completed without error, but the t) ; every size up to the maximum matched the CPU checksums (imageblock round trip through neighbour reads) and no larger size worked again

benchmarks.notes: tile_32x32 first refusal at 28 B/pixel: pipeline created and pass completed without error, but the tile kernel did not run (all pixels still hold the 0xCD sentinel); tile_32x16 first refusal at 60 B/pixel: pipeline created and pass completed without error, but the tile kernel did not run (all pixels still hold the 0xCD sentinel); tile_16x16 first refusal at 60 B/pixel: pipeline created and pass completed without error, but the tile kernel did not run (all pixels still hold the 0xCD sentinel); K = 4 bytes words per pixel, explicit imageblock<struct, imageblock_layout_explicit>; the sizes are the generated set 4..256 B; the time of a tile pass includes work proportional to K (write and read K words per pixel)

benchmarks.notes: scene: 1002528-triangle terrain BLAS + 1000 instances of a 200-triangle BLAS in one TLAS; 2048x2048 = 4.19 M rays per run; coherent = pinhole camera (one ray per pixel), incoherent = random origin/direction; alpha-test = 25% of the primitives rejected (intersection function table for the intersector, inline in the query loop); the CPU re-traces 256 dumped rays per variant. Apple10-only RT features (hardware instance transforms, IFB indexing) cannot be toggled: the same path runs on Apple9

TLAS = instances of one 200-triangle BLAS via indirect instance descriptors (BLAS ResourceID)
